title: Phase diagram and metastability of the Ising model on two coupled networks
central_claims: Two ferromagnetically coupled sparse Erdos-Renyi Ising networks have an aligned equilibrium state and a discontinuously appearing anti-aligned metastable state, with phase boundaries determined by replica free energy.
Metastable escape times follow Vogel-Fulcher-like temperature behavior and grow exponentially with network size, producing thermodynamic-limit trapping.

source_manifest.title: Phase diagram and metastability of the Ising model on two coupled networks
source_manifest.finding: Replica free energy and population dynamics characterize two coupled sparse random graphs. Metropolis simulations support the phase diagram and thermodynamic-limit metastable trapping.

source_manifest.title: Biswas-Chatterjee-Sen kinetic exchange opinion model for two connected groups
source_manifest.finding: Independent preprint later published in Physical Review E in 2025. It cites the Ising paper among precedents for opposing group order, then derives a different three-state annealed-interaction model. It does not reproduce the sparse-graph free energy or escape law.

source_manifest.title: A Majority-Vote Model On Multiplex Networks with Community Structure
source_manifest.finding: Peng and Porter cite the original as an example of opinion clusters in modular Ising networks. Their main construction extends majority-vote dynamics with layer preference, not the original replica solution.

source_manifest.title: Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model for spin glasses: Solution via the distributional zeta function method
source_manifest.finding: The conclusion names multiplex critical phenomena, citing the original, as a possible future application. That application is not performed in the paper.

answers.rationale: Later primary papers cite modular opposing-order phenomena, but none read explicitly verifies the original sparse-graph free-energy and metastability claims.
No independent reconstruction of the phase boundaries or Vogel-Fulcher-like escape behavior was verified.
The BChS and majority-vote studies change the dynamics and network assumptions; they are not stricter tests of this Ising result.
Related-model introductions retain broad coexistence background, but no authoritative assessment of the specific stability and escape-law contribution was found.
No follow-up explicitly tests the finite-size extrapolation or robustness of the replica solution beyond the stated graph ensemble.
The independent papers extend their own kinetic-exchange or majority-vote models; a substantive extension of this specific replica/metastability construction was not established.
Several teams cite the work, but two independent groups demonstrably building on its particular construction were not verified.
The later calculations use different mean-field or zeta-function methods and do not demonstrably reuse the original equations or population-dynamics implementation.
The zeta-function paper proposes a future application; no later review identifies this contribution as having enabled a research direction.
No read independent study uses the original phase diagram or escape times as an actual quantitative benchmark.
A concrete independent benefit from applying the original sparse-network solution was not demonstrated in the sources read.
Related opinion models show similar states, but successful application of this contribution outside its original graph setting was not verified.
The later papers derive new results, but their methods do not establish dependence on this particular Ising solution.
No use of this specific model in a deployed simulation, decision workflow or standard was verified; theoretical relevance alone does not demonstrate adoption.
No independent fair comparison verifies the original improvement over naive mean-field treatment at finite connectivity.
Later citations exceed three years, but the verified contexts are background and proposed future work rather than substantive reuse of the central construction.
The 2024 BChS preprint treats opposite group ordering as known, but does not assess the original exact phase diagram or escape-time law.
Citations occur in multiple later years, but substantive independent follow-up of the specific contribution was not established in two years.
No independent research synthesis adopting the specific phase diagram and metastable escape result as validated was verified.
No source explicitly demonstrates usefulness of this solution despite newer network or opinion-model alternatives.

search_gaps: No independent reproduction of the phase diagram or escape-time law was located.
The related BChS study was read as its 2024 preprint; its 2025 publication identity was verified separately.
The Peng thesis PDF could not be downloaded, but the associated majority-vote preprint was read.
The sparse-block-matrix citation-index lead did not yield a matching citation in the accessible preprint; it is not treated as outcome evidence.
research.summary: Independent papers cite the model as background for opposing group opinions or as a possible future application. The retrieved literature does not establish independent reproduction or concrete reuse of its exact sparse-network phase diagram and escape law. All outcomes remain unknown rather than negative.
